The Hebrew says the small one for a hundred and the great one for a thousand; BSB explicitly interprets this as each being a match for that many men.
The Hebrew names all the valleys as the object of putting to flight; BSB supplies the people in them.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew asks that God see and judge without explicitly identifying the object of judgment; BSB supplies you.
The Hebrew says the Spirit clothed Amasai and uses singular helper and a completed form of helped; BSB says the Spirit came upon him and uses plural helpers and present helps.
The Hebrew leaves the Philistines unnamed as recipients of help and leaves David unnamed as the one sent away; BSB supplies both names.
The Hebrew leaves the traveler unnamed; BSB identifies him as David.
The Hebrew says they became commanders in the army; BSB says they were commanders.
The Hebrew leaves the arriving men implicit and twice uses camp; BSB explicitly supplies men and twice uses army.
The Hebrew speaks of the LORD’s mouth; BSB uses His word.

The Hebrew calls the family his father’s house; BSB uses his own family.

The Hebrew calls them men of names in their fathers’ house; BSB says famous among their own clans.
